topics: Pricing models: per-token vs reserved capacity
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-01-17
- Start: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Jesse Huang (Redwood AE), Rosa Kim (Redwood SE), Andre Lawson (Redwood CSM), Priya Sharma (Novus Procurement), Ethan Miles (Novus Legal), Marco Velez (Novus CTO), Lydia Park (Novus Security)

Summary: (auto) quick notes - procurement priority, security gating, want clear cost path.

[00:00] Jesse Huang: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jesse with Redwood, AE. I'll hand off to Rosa for the technical overview but first quick agenda: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA/pricing models, private deployment options, KMS, pilot timeline.

[00:35] Priya Sharma: Thanks Jesse. We'll be brief on our side — procurement needs clarity on signing authority and cost buckets. Ethan is on for the legal bits and Lydia for security. Marco is here to ask about deployment constraints.

[01:12] Rosa Kim: Great. Very quickly, Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. For Novus we think hybrid might be sensible — private control plane with option to burst to dedicated in Redwood's region. That lowers up-front cost but keeps guardrails.

[01:50] Marco Velez: Can you clarify what you mean by burst? Like, if we exceed throughput on private, will requests go to hosted? We have strict data residency rules.

[02:05] Rosa Kim: Yes so policy-based routing. You can opt out of cross-region fallbacks; for regulated data we can keep everything inside your VPC or on-prem box. The burst to Redwood's dedicated pool would be optional and only for non-PHI flows, unless you sign off on data egress.

[02:40] Lydia Park: That sounds good. But explain KMS: we need customer-managed keys, HSM-backed, and proof that keys never leave our control. Is Bring-Your-Own-Key supported?

[02:58] Andre Lawson: Short answer yes, BYOK with cloud KMS integrations is supported, and we also support HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments. We'll need an HSM conversation for on-prem. We'll share an architecture doc.

[03:25] Ethan Miles: On the MSA/DPA — our legal team will want explicit language around data ownership, deletion on request, retention, and audit logs. Do you have precedent language for financial customers?

[03:40] Jesse Huang: We do. We'll produce an MSA with a financials appendix example, and we can highlight the DPA clauses. We typically accept a few redlines; major structural changes we flag for exec review. We'll send our standard SOC2 + ISO pack as well.

[04:10] Priya Sharma: Procurement will expect a clear SLA matrix with penalties. Uptime, response windows for P1 incidents, RTO/RPO?

[04:25] Rosa Kim: Our Dedicated product has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. For Private deployments we can offer an enterprise SLA if you take the support tier. We can map SLOs to incident severity, e.g., P1 response 15 minutes, P2 1 hour, with escalation paths.

[05:00] Marco Velez: Pricing - we're trying to compare per-token hosted pricing vs a reserved instance for steady throughput. If we commit monthly, what's the delta? Also curious about egress/network fees for VPC.

[05:22] Jesse Huang: Typical approach: per-token for hosted (good for variable/low volume), reserved capacity for predictable volumes (monthly commitments reduce unit cost). For VPC there's a network egress pass-through in some cloud setups — we can model that. We'll share a pricing spreadsheet with scenarios: 1) hosted pay-as-you-go, 2) reserved dedicated, 3) private with reserved infra plus support.

[05:55] Priya Sharma: Can you model a hybrid where low-sensitivity requests go to hosted (cheaper) and sensitive ones stay in private? And show cost delta?

[06:10] Rosa Kim: Absolutely. That's routing by policy — we can implement headers or tenant tags and route by sensitivity classification. The runtime supports prefix/KV cache so you save on token costs for repeated prompts. Note — caching behavior is different in private vs hosted because of shared caches.

[06:40] Ethan Miles: Back to DPA: can we include clause for data deletion and certificated deletion within X days, and logging for all requests including token-level logs? Also redaction controls?

[06:55] Andre Lawson: We can provide configurable retention windows and audit logs. Token-level logs are available in hosted mode with role-based access. For Private we can ship logs to your SIEM; retention is your config. We'll include sample retention templates.

[07:30] Marco Velez: Latency: our product needs 95th percentile under 250ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on dedicated?

[07:45] Rosa Kim: For short prompts Dedicated is the best fit; our benchmark profile shows sub-200ms p95 for the model tier we recommend (we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet). For Private performance depends on your hardware selection; we can recommend GPU SKUs.

[08:10] Priya Sharma: Any compliance badges we can have in the MSA? Like SOC 2 attestation, ISO, penetration test summaries?

[08:25] Andre Lawson: Yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert references, third-party pentest summary, and FedRAMP pathway notes (if needed). We'll share links to the security pack.

[09:00] Jesse Huang: Quick note — competitors sometimes push lower price but with opaque latency and no private/HSM options. Anthropic and other vendors were mentioned, but Redwood's differentiation here is the hybrid routing and clear SLA/observability.

[09:30] Lydia Park: On encryption in transit — TLS is table stakes, but we also need mTLS, per-service identity, and key rotation policies. How do you handle key rotation without service disruption?

[09:52] Rosa Kim: We support zero-downtime key rotation via dual-key acceptance windows in our private agent, plus rotation orchestration for cloud KMS. We'll provide a runbook.

[10:20] Ethan Miles: Regarding legal — will your DPA accept data processor terms we propose, or do you prefer to counter? We try to keep indemnities limited.

[10:36] Jesse Huang: We've accepted customer-proposed DPA redlines before; it depends on the scope. We'll take your proposed language back to our legal and flag any high-risk asks. Typical negotiations center on liability caps and data breach obligations.

[11:05] Marco Velez: Pilot — we want a 6-week pilot with 500k tokens/month, two models (chat + embeddings), and success criteria around latency, accuracy (compared to our baseline), and cost per inference. Can Redwood support model pinning and rollbacks during pilot?

[11:30] Rosa Kim: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies are supported. You can pin to a specific model version and do canary rollouts. For accuracy testing we recommend integrating Redwood's eval hooks. We'll also enable tracing and per-route metrics for the pilot.

[12:05] Priya Sharma: From procurement perspective, timeline? Our quarter close is end of Feb; we'd like contracts signed before that. Is that feasible?

[12:20] Jesse Huang: Yes, if procurement receives the redline MSA this week and security pack next week, legal and security review can be done in parallel. We usually see a 2-6 week cycle depending on redlines.

[12:45] Ethan Miles: A couple of specific redline asks: 1) include an audit right with 30 days' notice, 2) data breach notification within 72 hours, 3) liability cap tied to fees. We'll put these in a 1st-pass redline doc.

[13:10] Andre Lawson: That works — we'll look for the doc. Also note some customers want DPA carve-outs for aggregated telemetry used to improve models; we can provide opt-outs.

[13:45] Priya Sharma: About billing — can you provide invoice-level breakdowns by route/model for chargeback? Our finance team will need per-team cost visibility.

[14:00] Jesse Huang: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per API key/route/model, plus exportable CSVs for FinOps. We'll share a console demo link and sample export.

[14:25] Marco Velez: Regarding network architecture — if we go private in our VPC, what's required? NAT or peering? Are there firewall requirements?

[14:40] Rosa Kim: Two modes: private agent inside your VPC (no egress) or VPC peering for managed infra. For private agent you'll host a small runtime that communicates via controlled ports; we can provide Terraform modules. For peering there are egress configs to model. We'll send a network checklist.

[15:12] Lydia Park: Egress: how do you charge for data leaving our VPC? We have data transfer caps and financial controls.

[15:25] Jesse Huang: Egress costs depend on cloud provider and whether you use peering vs public egress. In many deals we model egress as pass-through to the customer. We'll include egress assumptions in the pricing scenarios.

[16:00] Ethan Miles: Can you confirm deletion of logs on contract termination and an escrow/exit plan for model weights if using Redwood-hosted model variants?

[16:15] Rosa Kim: We'll draft an exit plan: data deletion certs, key rotation steps, and export of customer-owned artifacts. For model weights, we provide a list of model variants and recommend model governance — if you need on-prem model we can arrange.

[16:50] Priya Sharma: Two more procurement asks: 1) Can we get a 60-day trial or credit for the pilot? 2) Are there standard payment terms?

[17:05] Jesse Huang: We usually offer pilot credits; terms are negotiable. Standard payment is net 30 for enterprise customers, but we can discuss net 45 in some cases.

[17:40] Marco Velez: For pilot evaluation we'll need a fixed test harness to compare latency and token usage. Do you provide a benchmarking harness?

[17:55] Rosa Kim: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness and the model inference traces. We'll also recommend prompt engineering to be consistent across runs.

[18:30] Priya Sharma: On SSO — can you support SAML-based SSO and role mapping for audit purposes?

[18:45] Andre Lawson: Yes, SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC are supported in the console. We'll provide an IdP integration guide.

[19:10] Ethan Miles: On e-discovery — we need a mechanism to export interaction logs tied to subject requests. How granular are your exports?

[19:25] Rosa Kim: You can export request-level logs, timestamps, and model output. For privacy we can mask or redact content depending on retention settings.

[20:00] Jesse Huang: I want to call out a few edge cases: 1) KV cache behavior in multi-tenant hosted environment, 2) rollbacks in canary deploys, 3) patching and maintenance windows for private agents. We'll include operational runbooks.

[20:40] Marco Velez: The KV cache - is that per-tenant, and how do we ensure no leakage?

[20:55] Rosa Kim: Cache is per-tenant. For hosted we shard caches by tenant id. For private there's a local cache you control. We'll document consistency guarantees.

[21:25] Priya Sharma: Alright, let's talk schedule: request you send MSA redlines by Monday 2025-01-20, security pack by 2025-01-21, architecture by 2025-01-24, and security deep-dive week of 2025-01-23. Is that achievable?

[21:50] Jesse Huang: Yes, we're aligned. We'll send the redlines and security pack. Rosa will produce the architecture doc. Andre will surface SOC2 artifacts.

[22:20] Ethan Miles: Quick question on indemnities: will Redwood accept a reasonable liability cap referencing a multiple of fees rather than absolute? We'll propose language in our redline.

[22:35] Jesse Huang: We'll review. Many customers accept a fees-based cap; we'll flag if legal deems it higher risk.

[23:00] (several brief clarifications, crosstalk)

[25:10] Rosa Kim: For the pilot we recommend these default resource profiles: small model for embeddings, medium chat model for prompt-response. We'll attach the exact SKU names in the doc; apologies if the auto-transcript munges model names like 'rvx-35b' into something else.

[26:00] Marco Velez: Noted. Also — can you confirm the logs we get do not include raw training telemetry? We need assurance telemetry is sanitized.

[26:18] Andre Lawson: Correct — telemetry we share is operational and request-level; we do not provide training telemetry. We'll provide a telemetry schema.

[28:00] Priya Sharma: Any concerns on our side? Marco: latency. Lydia: key management. Ethan: DPA liability. Priya: pricing and procurement timeline.

[28:20] Jesse Huang: Great. Let's recap next steps.

[28:35] Jesse Huang: Recap: 1) Jesse send MSA + DPA redlines and pricing scenarios; 2) Rosa send VPC/on-prem architecture + network checklist; 3) Andre send SOC2/ISO and security pack; 4) schedule security deep-dive w/ Lydia (week of 1/23); 5) Novus to provide redline DPA + procurement decision window.

[29:10] Priya Sharma: That matches. We'll aim to get legal redlines to you by 1/22.

[29:35] Ethan Miles: I'll prepare the redline doc and include the 72-hour breach clause, audit right, and liability cap ask.

[30:00] Jesse Huang: Perfect. Anything else before we wrap?

[30:10] Marco Velez: One last technical ask — can Redwood provide a runbook for disaster recovery for private agent?

[30:25] Rosa Kim: Yes, DR runbook and RTO/RPO guidance will be included.

[30:45] Priya Sharma: Okay good. Thanks all. We'll be in touch.

[57:30] (call ends, quick wrap)
